what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the tools in tools/check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts: what each tool does, what it takes and gives back, and how it runs.

payload.label: Check words or anything made against a person's own rules and verdicts
payload.job: Check words, a title, a script line or a plan against a person's own rules and the verdicts they already gave, and say pass, fail or uncertain for each, with why
payload.description: Give the units to check (each { text, kind } or { view, kind } for JSON such as a plan, with optional facts, field, context and findings you already have), rules (rule rows judge-words runs, and ask rows a model answers), and the person's own rule document (verdict_rules) and stands (stances, as tool:read-where-you-stand gives them), read from the records handed in (`records`) or the files given. Or give a branch in place of rules and verdict_rules: one of the person's branch rows (a node of kind branch in their one Checks list, list:checks, such as the kind of thing being made: a book, a script, an article, a post), and the rules are read from the records handed in: one tree in one list, every node naming the node it is part_of; the rows part_of that branch or a branch it is part_of, each branch read on its own (a branch below is never judged), plus the rows of every list a branch names in check_lists; step rows (questions of a decision step) and rows set Off are left out, a row that states no test (no words, pattern, exact, check, groups, path, evidence, ask or part) but says something is a reading row: a question a model answers once for each whole unit, made from the tool's own DATA over the row's words, carrying the calibration and model of the nearest branch's reading_settings, and listed in read_by_a_model; a piece of a source file, or a row that says nothing, is never judged: it is counted in rows_used.skipped.no_test, and a branch with only such rows answers no-applicable-rule; and the rows of the nearest branch carrying judge_settings (and of the branches extending it) are their verdict rows under those settings, the inherited rows generic rules. The answer then adds branch, lineage (nearest first) and rows_used. Their exact stand on a thing decides first: disagree fails, partly holds at review and fails at final, agree passes and clears the generic rules they named. Then their stated rows fail and their inferred rows (at_most uncertain) only hold. Nothing passes on silence: a thing nothing of theirs judges is novel, and an ask row never passes without a calibrated answer. The answer lists the questions a model may answer, by id; send the answers back in answers to use them. With branch the questions of a branch of hundreds of reading rows come in pages that each fit one answer: one entry for each rule (its ask said once, what every rule shares once in ask_all, a unit's own words never copied), and questions_page.next is the questions_after of the next call. Nothing about any person is built in.

branch.description: The id of one of the person's branch rows (a node of kind branch in list:checks) to check under, in place of rules and verdict_rules: the rows part_of it, and of every branch it is part_of, are read from the person's records

rules.description: Rule rows: judge-words rows (see tool:judge-against-rules), each optionally with held_when ({ path, where } over a unit's facts: its findings there only hold), or ask rows { id, kinds?, says, ask: { question, options, fail, at_most?, calibration: { status, t_pass, t_fail } } }

facts.description: Facts a row's when and held_when read, such as where the words came from

context_requires_review_rules.description: Rule ids whose findings need context review on this unit; only those findings become uncertain.

context_requires_review_checks.description: Named grammar checks whose findings need context review on this unit; other findings stay in force.

also_found.description: Findings you already have for this unit, each with outcome fail or uncertain

verdict_rules.description: The person's rule document: rows (judge-words rule rows; a row with part reads a part of a thing as another kind; a row with ask is a reading row a model answers), fold (how two texts are one text), stage.default (review or final), stance_rule and novel (the ids and words of the findings their stands and silence make) and agree_clears.rules (the generic rules their agree clears)

items.description: One stand, as tool:read-where-you-stand gives it: kind, artifact (1f: identity), text, contains or view, stance (agree, disagree, partly, or null when taken back), why (their own words) and at

rule.description: A rule id: with agree on an exact text, waives that one rule on that one line and judges nothing else

by.description: Who took the stand; only the person's (by person, or left out) waives a rule

stands.description: Where the person stands on things already made

stands_as_of.description: When the stands were read, if they were read from a copy and not live

questions_after.description: With branch: the questions_page.next of the last page of questions, for the next page; leave it out for the first. Send the same request otherwise, with the answers you have.

stage.description: review holds what final fails; the rule document's stage.default when left out

fields_by_kind.description: The field a unit of a kind is judged as, when the unit names none

answers.description: A model's answers by question id: { option: probability }

records.description: The rows the caller read from the person's own store (the engine keeps none), each { id, type, value }: record:check rows (the branch tree and its rules), the list rows a branch names in check_lists, and record:writing-voice rows. What is not given is not there. The run reads and writes no store.

questions.description: The questions a model may answer. With rules: one { id, rule, question, options, text } for each. With branch: one entry for each rule asked, { rule, question, ...ask, asked: [{ id, text? }] }, as many entries as fit one answer (see questions_page); a question is an entry over ask_all, and its text is the whole unit's (its result's) unless asked names one

questions_page.description: With branch: how many rules ask questions, how many entries this answer holds, and the questions_after of the next page (null on the last)

ask_all.description: With branch: the fields of the ask (options, fail, adapter, model, examples) that every rule has the same, said once for all the entries of questions

branch.description: With branch: the branch checked under

lineage.description: With branch: the branch and every branch it is part_of, nearest first

rows_used.description: With branch: the check rows read for each branch of the lineage, the rows of each check list read, and how many were left out as step rows, Off, or rows that neither state a test nor say anything (no_test)

read_by_a_model.description: With branch: the reading rows asked (rows that state no test but say something, each asked once a unit in questions): at most a bounded number of rows, how many more there are, and the branch whose reading_settings gave their calibration (null when none did)

provenance.source: a copy gate made generic: the person's rules, verdicts and words are input, never kept here

payload.label: Make labelled examples from where a person stands
payload.job: Turn the verdicts a person already gave into good and bad examples, to tune a model that answers their reading rules
payload.description: Give the person's rule document (verdict_rules) and their stands. Every thing of a reading row's kinds whose current stand is their exact agree is a good example; a stand a reading row names in pairs[].rejected is a bad example for that row. A pair naming no current exact stand is refused.

verdict_rules.description: The person's rule document: rows (judge-words rule rows; a row with part reads a part of a thing as another kind; a row with ask is a reading row a model answers), fold (how two texts are one text), stage.default (review or final), stance_rule and novel (the ids and words of the findings their stands and silence make) and agree_clears.rules (the generic rules their agree clears)

items.description: One stand, as tool:read-where-you-stand gives it: kind, artifact (1f: identity), text, contains or view, stance (agree, disagree, partly, or null when taken back), why (their own words) and at

payload.label: Check copy before a person reads it
payload.job: Check text, Markdown, pages, JSON, decks and picture readings against the rules you send, and the whole set against your required lines, audience, offers and counts, and say pass, fail, held or uncertain for each unit
payload.description: Give words as text, texts, Markdown, value (any JSON; fields names which keys hold words, or "strings" for every string), units, sources (JSON with its place), html (pages), decks (a rendered deck's HTML) or pictures with their readings. Markdown reads headings, paragraphs, list items, table cells and fenced display text; unresolved quotes, preamble before a declared document title and unsupported blocks stay coverage problems. It retains each block's role and field; for findings whose context is not established, name the matching rule ids or grammar check names for review, which keeps those findings uncertain and leaves other findings in force. Give rules (one row each: words, pattern, exact or a named grammar check) or leave them out to use mechanical grammar rows. Optionally give required (locked lines, features, baseline ids, approvals with the person's own words and the text they sit in), audience, offers and counts, and the person's verdict_rules and stands. Nothing about any person is kept here; their rules are input. A source with no words, a required line gone, a row for the wrong audience, a count that is not a published list view, an offer listing fewer lines than the others and a picture with no reading are problems, never passes. Model questions come back as questions; send answers on a second run.

rules.description: Rule rows, as tool:judge-against-rules takes them, with an optional not_for_kinds list. Left out: mechanical grammar rows.

kind.description: The kind of every word that names none (default copy)

fields.description: Markdown block role to source field mapping, such as heading to title and paragraph to body

context_requires_review_rules.description: Rule ids whose findings need context review on every Markdown unit in this document

markdown.description: Markdown documents: { text, where, kind, heading_kind, display_kind, document_heading_level, document_heading_is_metadata, quote_kind, fields, context_requires_review_rules }. Unresolved quotes and unsupported blocks are coverage problems; sentence-specific check findings on headings, list items, table cells and display text stay uncertain for context review.

value.description: Any JSON whose strings a person reads

fields.description: Which keys of value hold words, or "strings"

units.description: Ready-made units: { text, kind, where, facts }

sources.description: JSON with its place: { where, json, skip_keys, kind }

alt_keys.description: Keys whose strings are picture descriptions (kind alt)

sections.description: Markdown made of declared sections: { text, where, profile: { title_kind, sections: [{ heading, kind, heading_kind?, keeps_headings? }], required?, fields? } }. Preamble and source quotes are counted and never judged; an unknown section, a missing required section, a missing title or an empty body is a problem.

cue_narration.description: Narration split into cue headings: { text, where, profile: { kind, field?, cue_heading_level, cue_id_pattern, frontmatter?: { fields: { name: string|number }, required? } } }. Each unit keeps its cue_id; quotes, code, lists, text outside a cue, empty or repeated cues and unreadable frontmatter are problems.

json_roles.description: JSON whose words an owner declares: { json, where, owner: { paths, kind, field?, roles?: [{ paths, kind, field, context_requires_review? }] } }. Only the owner's paths are read; a string two roles claim, or that no role claims, is a problem.

readings.description: The words each picture shows, by the BLAKE3 of its bytes: { <blake3>: { text } }

kind_aliases.description: A kind a row names also covers these kinds

not_for_kinds.description: By row id: kinds the row does not judge

facts.description: Facts every unit carries for rows that read them

payload.label: Split a document into its pieces
payload.job: Split a document into its smallest self-contained pieces, a page per call, so every check can name the piece it came from
payload.description: Give one of the person's files by name (as /folder/file.md, read through their files door page by page, so a file of any size up to 4 MB is never sent in one request body), or the text of a short document (Markdown), and optionally its file name and its identity. Each paragraph, list item, table row or fenced block (``` or ~~~, as CommonMark fences them) under its headings is one piece; titles, rules and table headers are not. The answer holds the pieces and keeps nothing: each is a row shaped for the person's Checks list (id piece- and the first 24 hex of its identity, kind piece) with says (its lead), text, identity (1f: and the BLAKE3 of its whitespace-folded text), key (its heading path and lead), sources (the file, the piece's key there as section, the file identity and the line where it starts), and empty tags, kinds and checked_by; the same text twice is one piece with two sources. Pieces come a page per call within most_bytes (the door carries an answer twice in one 64 KiB message): send the answer's next as after to read the next page. A piece too large for one answer is named in too_large. The person's AI keeps the pieces in the store of its choice; tool:check-every-piece-is-covered then says what each kept piece lacks.

name.description: The name of one of the person's files to split, as /folder/file.md, read by reference through their files door

text.description: The words of a short document, as Markdown, in place of name (a request body over 64 KiB is refused by the door: send name for a larger file)

file.description: The document's name kept in each piece's sources; name when left out

file_identity.description: The document's identity (1f: and 64 hex); the identity of its bytes when left out

after.description: The next of the answer before: the id of the last piece of the page before; the first page when left out

most_bytes.description: The most bytes of JSON the answer takes (28000 when left out)

stored.description: What this run reads of the person's own things, read by the caller from where the person keeps them (the engine keeps none) and given here: files: {name: text or {base64}} under /, as this row's `stored` lists. What is not given is not there.

total.description: The pieces of the whole document, one per identity

pieces.description: This page's piece rows, in reading order

next.description: Send as after for the next page; null on the last

needs._what: memory_mb is the run's peak resident memory at its largest declared input, a file of 4 MiB less 4 KiB (the most the row reads: 4,194,304 bytes), measured by at-the-size-of-a-real-list.test.mjs: 299 and 316 MB on two runs under the test's heap cap (memory_mb less 80 = 304 MB), and 370 MB with no heap cap. The row declared 128, which the largest input exceeds: its heap ran out at 48 MB and never finished. 384 is the measured peak rounded up to the next 128 MB, the step these rows declare in. The engine enforces a run's memory as its physical footprint (src/tool_runs/os.rs group_footprint, against invoke.max_memory_bytes), so this figure is the resident size, not the heap.

payload.label: Check every piece of a person's files has a check or a reason
payload.job: Say, for each of a person's source files, how many of its pieces have a check, how many a recorded reason, and which are uncovered
payload.description: Reads the Checks rows handed in as records (the person's AI reads them from its own store: the ids of their Checks list and its rows whose kind is piece, as tool:split-a-document-into-pieces kept them, without their text), folding each piece into a running tally, so the run holds counts and a bounded number of named pieces. The run reads and writes no store. A piece is covered when checked_by names check rows that all exist, or when no_check has a reason (and every row its covered_by names exists). The answer: totals over every file, and per source file its pieces, those with a check, those with a reason and how many are uncovered, naming the first uncovered pieces by id, section and lead; status failed when any piece is uncovered. Checks and covered_by naming rows that do not exist are counted and the first named. The answer fits at most most_bytes of JSON: when more files remain, next is the after of the next page; with file, the page names that file's uncovered pieces by id, after after. Nothing is written.

file.description: One source file: its counts and its uncovered pieces by id, page by page

after.description: The next of the answer before: the last file shown (over every file) or the last piece named (with file)

most_bytes.description: The most bytes of JSON the answer takes (28000 when left out)

records.description: The record:check rows the caller read from the person's own store (their Checks list: the check rows and the piece rows; a piece's text may be left out, the coverage does not read it), each { id, type, value }. What is not given is not there. The run reads and writes no store.

needs._what: memory_mb is the run's peak resident memory at the largest list the row is handed, the 40,707-row Checks list (39,088 pieces) given as the input's records: 157 MB at 512 MB and 185 MB at 256 MB, measured by at-the-size-of-a-real-list.test.mjs (Nov 19, 2026), under the test's heap cap of memory_mb less 80. 256 is the next container step above the measured peak; the test asserts the peak stays under memory_mb.

payload.label: Check a film's copy against a person's rules and verdicts
payload.job: Check every line of a film's copy files (a script table, titles, cards, a post, a description, prose or narration) against the person's own branch of their checks, with their film readers and settings
payload.description: Takes the person's settings row for this tool (list:settings, the record itself as settings_record) and reads the rules of one branch of their one Checks list (its own rows and every row of the branches above it; the nearest branch with judge_settings makes their verdict rows) from the records handed in (`records`; the run reads no store). Reads the lines of each file handed in by the layouts their settings name (Markdown table columns by file name, fenced post text, blockquotes, paragraph files, plain lines, JSON lines), or by a declared reader (sectioned prose, cue narration, a JSON owner's paths). Marks a line the person's own recorded words when every word is in a recording span the piece's plan cites, so a row written for added words only holds there; attaches each line's context and the reader-knowledge findings it is handed. Answers per line pass, fail or uncertain with every finding, the questions a model should answer by id (send them back as answers), the report with the BLAKE3 identity of each file, the reader settings, the rules and the checker, and exit_code (0 passed, 1 failed, 2 unqualified, 3 uncertain). Nothing is written.

branch.description: The id of one of the person's branch rows of list:checks, such as content-production

settings_record.description: The person's list:settings row for this tool, record:setting:check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>, as the person's store holds it, { id, type, value }: the film readers, spans, profiles, owners, fields, origin words and reader-knowledge rows. Your AI reads it and gives it here; an id alone is refused.

plan.description: The plan the lines' cut was built from, by name in plans

plans.description: Plans by name: the one named by plan or by a piece's plan line

recordings.description: The word lists by clip and the moment rows of the clips the plans cite

reader_knowledge.description: { findings } from do-work/reader_knowledge.py over the reading units, or { not_run: why }

records.description: The rows the caller read from the person's own store (the engine keeps none), each { id, type, value }: the record:check rows and list rows of the branch, and the record:writing-voice rows. The settings row is given as settings_record itself. What is not given is not there. The run reads and writes no store.
